name: solidity-workbench
description: Auto-import, completion that understands your code, diagnostics while you type, hover and signature help with NatSpec, rename and references across the project, and Go to Definition for Solidity and Foundry projects.

solidityWorkbench.foundry.forgePath.markdownDescription: Path to the `forge` executable used to run `forge remappings`. With the default `forge`, the `PATH`, `$FOUNDRY_DIR/bin` and `~/.foundry/bin` are tried. When forge cannot be run, remappings are inferred from `remappings.txt`, `foundry.toml` and the library folders following forge's rules.

solidityWorkbench.index.includeTests.markdownDescription: Index the project test directory (`test` in `foundry.toml`).

solidityWorkbench.index.includeScripts.markdownDescription: Index the project script directory (`script` in `foundry.toml`).

solidityWorkbench.index.excludeLibTestsA.markdownDescription: Skip `test`, `tests`, `mock` and `mocks` folders inside library directories (`lib/`).

solidityWorkbench.index.exclude.markdownDescription: Glob patterns, relative to the project root, of Solidity files to leave out of the index. Example: `lib/**/certora/**`.

solidityWorkbench.completion.enabled.markdownDescription: Suggest Solidity types and keywords for the context, variables and parameters in scope, contract members (including inherited ones), struct fields in `S({...})`, members after `.` (`msg.sender`, `block.timestamp`, address and array members, struct fields...) and global functions, according to the file's solc version. May duplicate completions from other Solidity extensions.

solidityWorkbench.autoImport.enabled.markdownDescription: Suggest symbols from the project and its dependencies in completions and add the import automatically.

enumDescriptions: Use the remapped path (e.g. `@openzeppelin/contracts/access/Ownable.sol`) when a remapping covers the file, else a relative path.
Always use a path relative to the importing file.
solidityWorkbench.autoImport.pathStyle.markdownDescription: Style of the paths written in new imports.

solidityWorkbench.syntaxDiagnostics.enab.markdownDescription: Report syntax errors while typing: unbalanced brackets (pointing at the block that was left open), misspelled keywords such as `contact` (with a quick fix) and parser errors. May conflict with diagnostics from other Solidity extensions.

solidityWorkbench.outline.enabled.markdownDescription: Provide the document outline (Outline view, breadcrumbs, Go to Symbol in Editor) for Solidity files.

solidityWorkbench.hover.enabled.markdownDescription: Show what the name under the mouse is: the signature and NatSpec of variables, parameters, functions, events, errors, structs, enums and contracts of the project (inherited and imported ones included), and the type and documentation of built-in globals and members (`msg.sender`, `block.timestamp`, `abi.encode`, `keccak256`, units...) according to the file's solc version. Never runs solc. May duplicate hovers from other Solidity extensions.

solidityWorkbench.signatureHelp.enabled.markdownDescription: Show the parameters of the call being written, with the NatSpec of the declaration and of each parameter: project functions and members (functions attached with `using ... for` included), events after `emit`, errors after `revert`, struct constructors (`S(...)`, `S({...})`), `new C(...)`, modifiers and base constructors, and built-in functions (`require`, `abi.encode`, `keccak256`...). The overload the arguments can reach is selected. Never runs solc. May duplicate signature help from other Solidity extensions.

solidityWorkbench.navigation.enabled.markdownDescription: Go to Definition (including local variables, inherited members, aliases, `Library.member` and members of values such as `token.transfer` or `listing.price`), Find All References and Document Highlight (using solc's AST for anything that is not a local), clickable import paths and Go to Symbol in Workspace. May conflict with navigation from other Solidity extensions.

solidityWorkbench.rename.enabled.markdownDescription: Rename Symbol (F2). Local variables and parameters are renamed instantly, respecting blocks and shadowing; everything else (state variables, functions with their overrides, modifiers, events, errors, structs and fields, enums, types, contracts and their file) is renamed across `src`, `test` and `script` using solc's AST, and the result is checked by compiling it again. Refused when the project does not compile or the symbol is declared in `lib/`. May conflict with renaming from other Solidity extensions.

solidityWorkbench.formatting.enabled.markdownDescription: Format Solidity files with `forge fmt`, using the `[fmt]` section of `foundry.toml`. Off by default: enable it and pick Solidity Workbench as the formatter (`editor.defaultFormatter`) if you want Format Document or format on save to use it.

solidityWorkbench.compilerDiagnostics.en.markdownDescription: Check Solidity files with solc while typing, including unsaved changes: type errors, missing constructor arguments, unknown identifiers, warnings... Results are filtered like `forge build` (`ignored_error_codes`, `ignored_warnings_from`, nothing from libraries). May conflict with diagnostics from other Solidity extensions.

solidityWorkbench.compilerDiagnostics.de.markdownDescription: Milliseconds to wait after the last keystroke before running solc.

solidityWorkbench.compilerDiagnostics.ig.markdownDescription: Extra solc warning codes to hide, as numbers (`2072`) or foundry names (`"unused-var"`). Added to `ignored_error_codes` from `foundry.toml`. Errors are never hidden.

solidityWorkbench.compiler.solcPath.markdownDescription: solc to use instead of the automatic choice: a path to a binary, or a version installed by forge (`0.8.30`). By default the `solc` of `foundry.toml`, or the newest installed version that satisfies the file's `pragma`, is used.

scripts.test: npm run test:unit && npm run test:integration
scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run typecheck && npm run build:prod
